page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using KVM virtualization. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon Skylake 8163 processors operating at 2.5 GHz, it features 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled to provide 24 virtual CPUs. The system is equipped with 48 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for compute-heavy applications. Cache specifications include 32 KB L1d and 1.0 MB L2 per core, along with 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Hardware acceleration support includes AVX-512, AES, and FMA instructions. The instance does not include local ephemeral SSD storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmark results indicate solid multi-threaded capability alongside lower single-core throughput. Single-core stress-ng scores of 1106.0 and Geekbench single-core scores of 991.0 demonstrate modest per-core performance, which impacts single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks show reliable resource scaling, recording 17696.41 in multi-core stress-ng and 18382.84 in PassMark CPU tests. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 96.87 GB/sec while write bandwidth measures 52.35 GB/sec, supporting steady execution for parallelized applications and in-memory datastores like Redis.

The hardware configuration provides high vCPU allocation without adding unnecessary memory overhead or bundled local drive costs. Primary operational tradeoffs include moderate single-threaded clock speed and mandatory reliance on cloud storage volumes for disk storage. The resource layout aligns effectively with multi-threaded web serving, parallel software compilation, batch processing, and small-model inference tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 24 vCPUs across 12 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores at 2.5 GHz and 48 GB of memory. Operating under KVM virtualization without bundled local drives or integrated GPUs, it features instruction set support for AVX-512, AES, and FMA, backed by an 8 Gbps baseline network connection. Benchmark evaluations show solid multi-core execution, achieving 17696.41 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 13.48 GB/sec static web serving throughput, alongside moderate single-core speeds. Its 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers a compute-dense configuration suitable for multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight model inference.
